Wait, let me look more carefully:
- Before: red rectangle was at [30,12]-[33,17] (id=14 in earlier frames, R, 24 pixels)
- After: red rectangle is at [24,18]-[29,21] (id=11, R, 24 pixels)
So the red rectangle moved from the middle-left position up to near the blue square. The red rectangle was originally below the blue square, and now it's above the dark red square.
Also, the white frames on the right turned black. This might mean the "target" was consumed or completed.
Let me also note:
- The blue square (id=8, b, 16 pixels) is at [20,18]-[23,21]
- The red rectangle (id=11, R, 24 pixels) is now at [24,18]-[29,21] - directly below the blue square
- The dark red square (id=14, r, 16 pixels) is at [30,18]-[33,21] - below the red rectangle
So the red rectangle moved up to be adjacent to the blue square. This suggests that clicking on the red target on the right "activated" the red piece on the left, causing it to move.
But wait, the red target on the right is still there (id=5, R, 47 pixels). The frame around it changed from white to black though.
Let me think about the game mechanics:
- The right panel shows target shapes (red and blue)
- Clicking on a target on the right causes the corresponding colored piece on the left to move
- The goal might be to position the left pieces to match the right targets
Looking at the current image, the red rectangle is now stacked vertically with the blue square and dark red square. The right panel shows a red shape (top) and blue shape (bottom).
Maybe the game is about building the target shapes on the left by stacking the colored pieces. The red target on the right is a specific shape, and I need to arrange red pieces on the left to match it.

        regions['hud'].append((r, c, old, new))

        regions['right'].append((r, c, old, new))
print(f"Left changes: {len(regions['left'])}, Right changes: {len(regions['right'])}, HUD: {len(regions['hud'])}")
